baseline.name: Preallocated indexed alternating merge
baseline.approach: Measure lengths, allocate combined output and alternate characters using indices.
baseline.space: O(1) work state plus O(a+b) output

archived.name: Two read cursors and output cursor
archived.space: O(1) work state plus O(a+b) output

why: The archive is a conventional preallocated merge; separate tail loops handle unequal lengths cleanly.
quantitative_comparison: Both write exactly a+b characters and one terminator after length scans. No lower asymptotic work, output storage or measured constant-factor advantage is established.
tradeoffs: Requires valid terminated strings and safe length/allocation arithmetic. The checked output allocation belongs to the caller; code clarity is not a numeric speed metric.
evidence_basis: Static equivalence to an equally linear preallocated baseline; no runtime benchmark.
